title.narrative: Strengthening the quality compliance capacity of the honey value chain for greater market access

description.narrative: UNIDO concluded with the Norwegian Agency for Development Agency (Norad) in January 2019 the Global Market Access Programme (GMAP) 2020-2024. The integrated Programme specifically aims to enhance market access in prioritized value chains in selected countries (Colombia, Ethiopia, Malawi, Mozambique and Myanmar), by focusing on the following three components as agreed: 1. Enhanced technical competence and sustainability of the Quality Infrastructure 2. Enhanced SME compliance with standards and technical regulations 3. Strengthened culture for quality The GMAP will allow the honey sector in Ethiopia to be identified and selected as one of the country-specific projects according to due selection criteria and was incorporated into GMAP, as agreed with Norad. UNIDO (TII/SQI) thus took field mission and sent experts in June, September December 2018 to conduct investigation and assessment on key issues surrounding the honey value chain in 2019, including the key actors, the capacity of QI elements (standards, metrology, conformity assessment), technologies used in honey production and current programmes by national and international partners.
